s: Stores all state changes as an immutable append-only event log rather than overwriting current state.
w: Instead of UPDATE rows, you APPEND events (OrderCreated, ItemAdded, PaymentReceived). Current state is derived by replaying events. The event log is the source of truth; snapshots optimize replay for long histories. Projections build read-optimized views. Temporal queries answer 'what was the state at time T?'. Kafka or EventStoreDB serve as the log infrastructure.
use: Audit-critical domains: financial transactions, healthcare records, legal systems
Complex state machines: order lifecycle, insurance claims, approval workflows
Systems needing temporal queries and full history replay
Debugging production issues - the full history of what happened is available
avoid: Simple CRUD apps where current-state-only storage is sufficient
High-cardinality event streams with no meaningful state transitions
Teams without experience managing event schema evolution and projection rebuilding

props.event_store: Kafka | EventStoreDB | Postgres with append-only table

world: Kafka as event store at LinkedIn/Uber

pat.d: Events written to store; projections rebuild read models for querying.
Event-driven saga steps react to previously committed events.

pits: Event schema evolution breaking old projections - use upcasting and schema registry
Replay time growing unbounded - implement snapshots every N events
tips: Event sourcing and CQRS are complementary, not synonymous - distinguish them clearly
Event schema registry is essential for versioning - mention Avro or protobuf for event payloads
